speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I see you're experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To understand the cause, are these symptoms constant or do they come and go? Also, have you noticed any drooping eyelids or slurred speech?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of symptoms worsening with activity and improving with rest is very characteristic. Does the double vision affect both eyes equally, or is it worse in one eye? Also, have you noticed any difficulty swallowing or chewing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.
